title: Resilient partial-JSON reconstruction across streaming/toolcall boundaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When clients stream structured JSON that includes nested tool/function-call sections, partial token truncation and mid-stream retries frequently produce nonrecoverable payloads for clients that expect a single valid JSON doc. This is exacerbated by compatibility shims (older SDKs) that expect newline-delimited objects or length-prefixed frames.

Background: We support streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured outputs concurrently. In real traffic we see cases where a tool call starts inside one stream fragment, the model continues, the connection is interrupted, and on retry the regenerated tokens differ slightly (escaping, whitespace, or duplicated keys). Current server-side heuristics try naive concatenation or a simple bracket-balance repair which fails for interleaved tool-call markers or JSON with large string fields.

Goal: Provide a robust, deterministic server-side reconstruction and client-facing compatibility behavior that: (1) allows safe resumption/retries without corrupting downstream parsers, (2) supports older SDK expectations via optional framing modes, and (3) keeps latency and token-cost overhead minimal.

Scope: Design and implement a reconstruction layer in the streaming mux that understands token offsets, tool-call boundaries, and framing policies. Add a compatibility shim for newline-delimited and length-prefixed consumers. Add automated fuzz tests and integration tests for real-world partials.
acceptance_criteria: Server can reconstruct valid JSON 95%+ of time for simulated single-connection resumes with up to 15% token divergence compared to golden output
Clients using 'framemode=newline' receive NDJSON-compatible chunks when enabled; legacy SDKs can opt-in without parsing errors
Tool/function call boundaries are preserved; tool-call metadata (name, arguments) remain parseable after resume
Benchmark: additional median latency per resumed request < 10ms and token bill delta < 3% for typical webtext workloads
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering truncation inside strings, escaped characters, duplicated keys, and interleaved toolcalls
design_decisions: Use a three-stage server pipeline: (1) token-stream annotator (produces boundary markers and byte offsets), (2) fragment reconciler (uses heuristics + deterministic repair rules), (3) compatibility framer (NDJSON or length-prefixed mode)
Deterministic repair rules prioritized over permissive heuristics: prefer canonical escaping and schema-guided fills when possible
Keep default behavior conservative (reject irrecoverable fragments with explicit error) and provide optional aggressive backfill mode behind a feature flag
Do not rely on client-side replays for correctness; server-side must produce a reasonable single-document representation on resume when possible
tradeoffs: Aggressive repair can hide model regressions or prompt bugs; to mitigate, we emit structured diagnostics and store a traceable fragment diff for postmortem
Storing extra metadata (offsets, checksums) increases memory per request; we cap detailed traces to requests flagged for retries or high risk
Compatibility framing modes add maintenance surface area for SDKs; we will document and version the framing contracts and provide reference implementations
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy fragment annotator + non-destructive diagnostics in api-runtime-2.4-canary; enable for 1% of streaming traffic
Phase 2 (repair): enable default conservative repair for canary traffic and expose 'framemode' query param to opt-in NDJSON/length-prefixed
Phase 3 (backfill): enable aggressive backfill behind feature flag for customers with migration needs; monitor parsing errors and customer complaints
Phase 4: wide rollout after 2 weeks of canary telemetry and at least 10 successful recovery test scenarios
test_plan: Unit tests for annotator: token offset correctness, tool boundary tags, escape sequence annotation
Fuzz corpus derived from production streaming traces (sanitized) to emulate truncations within strings, escape sequences, and tool-call payloads
Integration test: simulated resume with token divergence (0-20%) verifying reconstructed JSON parses and matches schema validators
E2E: SDK clients (python/js) that use newline and length-prefixed framing validate round-trip parsing with resumed streams
Load test: measure latency and memory overhead with 5k concurrent streaming connections and 2% forced retries
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after paging incident response with examples of two truncated toolcall sessions. Assigned to Priya for implementation plan.

2026-03-11 Priya Rao: Spike completed — built a prototype annotator that tags token indices and emits minimal fragment metadata. Early results look promising; attached microbenchmarks show ~4ms overhead.

2026-03-12 Marco Hernandez (review): Reviewed heuristics. Suggest adding schema-aware merge for known models (eg. tool call arg types) and ensuring we never accidentally change user-visible strings except to fix escaping.
2026-03-12 Priya Rao: Implemented conservative repair and NDJSON framing toggle. Pushed draft PR for internal review: GH #2034. Added compatibility tests for python-sdk newline mode.

2026-03-13 QA (Elena Kim): Found a failing case where duplicated keys appear when model backfills slightly different object orders. Created follow-up subtask ENG-57803 to canonicalize object key order when schema permits.
